name: Nemotron 3.5 Lightning
tagline: NVIDIA's 293-tok/s execution-tier MoE ships weights, data, AND recipes — under OpenMDW again
description: A 30B-total / 3B-active hybrid that interleaves Mamba-2 and mixture-of-experts layers with select attention: 52 layers, 6 of 128 routed experts plus one shared expert per token, 1M-token context. Five checkpoints shipped at once — BF16 reference, NVFP4 deployment, the pre-trained Base, and two speculative-decoding draft variants — alongside the actual pre- and post-training datasets (Nemotron-CC-v2 at 9.1T tokens among them) and training recipes.
why: NVIDIA is refreshingly honest about what this is: an execution-tier model for tool calls and validation loops, not a peak-accuracy play — its own table shows Qwen 3.6 35B ahead on 13 of 14 rows while Lightning does 293 output tok/s, third-fastest of 134 models tracked by Artificial Analysis. And the release radius is the real story: weights, data, and recipes together is a level of reproducibility the big permissive-license labs still don't offer.
useCases: High-throughput agent execution loops — tool calls, validation, routing
1M-token context processing where speed matters more than peak accuracy
Reproducibility research: retrain or ablate against released data and recipes
audience: Agent-infra teams optimizing cost per call; open-training researchers

setup.requirements: ~60GB BF16 or the NVFP4 build for single-GPU serving; day-one GGUF via ggml-org, unsloth, and bartowski for local use

license.weights: OpenMDW-1.1; released datasets separately marked permissive for model training, most gated behind approval
license.notes: Same call as NVIDIA Cosmos 3 and Laguna S 2.1, same reasoning: OpenMDW-1.1 grants rights 'without restriction' with attribution-only conditions and a litigation-termination clause — substantively MIT-grade, no use restrictions, no output claims. But it is not OSI-approved, and our bright line is OSI approval, so we downgrade rather than round up. This is the third OpenMDW entry in the catalog; the precedent is now well worn. One gap to close by hand: the card states 'use of this model is governed by the OpenMDW-1.1 model license' and the repo is tagged accordingly, but HF rate-limited our file-tree check, so the standalone LICENSE file wants a 30-second browser confirmation. Checked 2026-08-17.

tally.stars: 156 HF likes across the checkpoint family in week one; ggml-org, unsloth, and bartowski GGUF repos live

limitations: It loses to same-class Qwen on nearly every quality benchmark by NVIDIA's own table — this is a speed play, full stop; most of the released datasets sit behind HF gating and approval; and OpenMDW, however permissive, still isn't the three-letter license your counsel already knows.
take: The most reproducible release of the week carries the asterisk, while less-forthcoming labs ship clean MIT. Our bright line stays put — but this is the entry that makes it feel expensive.
